newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas up in Q1 as 8 deals done at higher price.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas up in Q1 as 8 deals done at higher price.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices moved up in the first quarter on Wednesday as at least eight trades were done at higher prices there, dealers said. And the quarters on either side of Q1 moved up accordingly as the whole winter strengthened.
A single trader reported doing all eight trades in Q1, totalling 250,000 therms a day. Although the trader did not confirm being the buyer in every case, the market clearly believed that it had been.
All the trades were done between 16.10 pence and 16.20 pence a therm, when the market had been bid at 15.85 pence on Tuesday.
By the close Q1 was even stronger, bid at 16.15 pence against offers at 16.25 pence.

"They've chosen the dearest part of the curve to pull the whole curve up to sell their long position into it," said one trader, speculating on the reasons behind the buying spree. But this was just speculation, with the trader in question not commenting on the reasons behind the buying.

Otherwise the market was relatively quiet. Both Q4 and Q2 were stronger, and dealers said this was simply to maintain the differentials against Q1. Although Q2 was traded at 11.125 pence and 11.15 pence, it was assessed higher at the close. And Q4 was not heard trading on an outright basis, although October traded three times within the assessed range of Tuesday.

The prompt period was relatively active, and within day and day ahead prices remained firm, reflecting the high SAP on the flexibility mechanism. But dealers agreed that with the exception of Q1, the market was essentially quiet and there were no new market fundamentals influencing prices.

IPE futures mirrored the physical market, with the winter up significantly. The whole period from November through to next June settled higher, while the first three months and next July were lower, but only 50 lots were traded in two deals.

The budget cut the gas levy to zero from next April, a decision welcomed by Centrica plc which will be the main beneficiary. But road fuel gases saw their excise rate unchanged, although the industry was encouraged that at least the differential against gasoline and diesel has continued to widen.
